topics.description: Italian revolutionary, nationalist, and military leader who led the Redshirts in the conquest of Sicily and Naples during the unification of Italy.
aliases: The Hero of the Two Worlds

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This cause defeated the black nobility that supported the independence of Pius IX. A supporter of this cause wrote an open letter to Charles Albert and was a member of the Carbonari. In the Plombières Agreement, Napoleon III agreed to support this cause at the behest of Count Cavour. At the battle of Calatafimi, supporters of this cause called Redshirts defeated the Kingdom of the Two (*) Sicilies. This cause was accomplished when Victor Emmanuel II ascended the throne of a new country with the support of Giuseppe Garibaldi. For 10 points, name this nationalist cause to create a new kingdom led from Rome.
parts.answer: Italian Unification [accept word forms such as the unification of Italy; or the Risorgimento]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: To garner international support for this cause, Count Cavour entered Piedmont-Sardinia into the Crimean War. The success of this cause resulted in the crowning of Victor-Emmanuel II as king. The Red Shirts advanced this cause under (*) Giuseppi Garibaldi by conquering the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. For 10 points, what 19th century cause sought to consolidate provinces like the Papal States and Venice into a single country?
parts.answer: Italian Unification [or Risorgimento] <European History–Kapadia>

topics.description: The catastrophic 1986 explosion, fire, and radioactive release at reactor four of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Soviet Ukraine.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Tourism to this historic compound usually includes visits to the towns of Zalesye and Kopachi and a tour of the Red Forest. This compound’s New Safe Confinement was built in 2016 over a concrete sarcophagus around (*) reactor number four. This compound’s “elephant’s foot” was discovered by “liquidators” in 1986. For ten points, name this power plant near the town of Pripyat in Ukraine, the site of a massive nuclear disaster.
parts.answer: Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant (accept ChNPP; accept Vladimir Lenin Nuclear Power Plant)

topics.description: A period of dynastic crisis, political instability, foreign intervention, and competing claims to the Russian throne from 1598 to 1613.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler created a parliament called the Zemsky Sobor in 1549. Three people claimed to be this ruler’s dead youngest son, Dmitri, during the Time of Troubles. Peasants were terrorized and the city of (*) Novgorod was sacked by the Oprichniki, this ruler’s secret police. This man the epithet “Grozny” from acts like beating his own son to death. For ten points, name this first Tsar of All Russia, known as “the Terrible.”
parts.answer: Ivan the Terrible (accept Ivan IV Vasilyevich; accept Ivan the Fearsome, Ivan the Awesome, or anything similar; accept Ivan Grozny)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: After one holder of this position killed his son with a scepter in a fit of rage, this position saw a period of  instability that ended the Rurikid Dynasty’s control of it. Boris Gundunov was elected to this position before  the Time of Troubles, during which it was claimed by three (*) False Dmitrys. The last holder of this position  was forced to abdicate in the February Revolution of 1917, ending the Romanov Dynasty. For 10 points, identify  this royal position that ruled imperial Russia.
parts.answer: Tsar [or Czar; prompt on Ruler of Russia]

topics.description: A Southeast Asian country formerly known as Siam, with a constitutional monarchy established after the 1932 revolution and a history including the Ayutthaya and Chakri kingdoms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Marshal Phibun, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] After a 1932 coup in which Phibun came to power in this country governed from Bangkok, he changed its official name from Siam to a name meaning “land of the free.”
parts.answer: Thailand [or Kingdom of Thailand; or Ratcha-anachak Thai]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] After a failed monarchist revolt, Phibun installed to the throne a boy studying in Switzerland, Ananda Mahidol, who then gained this regnal name. The current king of Thailand also has this regnal name.
parts.answer: Rama [accept Rama VIII; accept Rama X]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During World War II, Phibun negotiated an alliance with this country, allowing its troops to pass through Thailand during the Burma Campaign.
parts.answer: Japan [or Nihon-koku; or Nippon-koku; or Empire of Japan; or Dai Nippon Teikoku; or Japanese Empire]

topics.description: A mysterious confederation of maritime raiders and migrants associated with attacks on eastern Mediterranean powers during the Bronze Age Collapse.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Much of the information about this group’s attempted conquest of Egypt was derived from inscriptions and reliefs at Medinet Habu. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this confederation of people, whose origin remains mysterious. This group contributed to the fall of empires like the Mycenaeans and Hittites during the Bronze Age Collapse.
parts.answer: Sea Peoples

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Sea Peoples may have allied with a group called “Ahiyyawa” from this country. According to Homer, a confederation from this modern-day country fought Troy in the Trojan War.
parts.answer: Greece [or the Hellenic Republic; or Ellas; or Elliniki Dhimokratia]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Unlike most Mediterranean polities, some Phoenician cities peaked after the Bronze Age collapse, such as this Tunisian city founded by Dido. This city’s army was once run by the Barca family.
parts.answer: Carthage [or Kart-hadasht; or Colonia Julia Carthago; or Karchedon]

topics.description: The Stuart monarch who ruled Scotland as James VI and England and Ireland as James I, succeeding Elizabeth I in 1603 and commissioning the King James Bible.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The spymaster Sir Francis Walsingham served as this monarch’s Secretary of State, and stopped the Ridolfi and Babbington plots that threatened this ruler. This monarch’s navy defeated an invasion attempt by Philip II [second] with the help of Sir (*) Francis Drake. Because this monarch died childless, James Stuart inherited the throne after her 1603 death. For ten points, name this final Tudor monarch of England, the sister of Mary I [first] and daughter of Henry VIII [eighth].
parts.answer: Elizabeth I [first] (prompt on “Elizabeth” or “Queen Elizabeth”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Wine-drunk monks would pee on this good before it was compressed as a damp paste in the process of corning. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this good possibly introduced to Europe after the Battle of Mohi. Robert Catesby fled London after 36 barrels of this good were discovered under Parliament on November 5th, 1605.
parts.answer: gunpowder [accept the Gunpowder Plot]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Gunpowder Plot was an attempt to kill the first Stuart king with this name, who commissioned an eponymous English translation of the Bible.
parts.answer: James [accept James I [“the first”]; accept King James Bible]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] An interactive exhibit in this location shows where Guy Fawkes confessed his participation in the Gunpowder Plot. Richard of Shrewsbury and Edward V were murdered in this location near the end of the War of the Roses.
parts.answer: Tower of London [prompt on the Tower; prompt on Princes in the Tower]

topics.description: The 1520 Spanish retreat from Tenochtitlan under Hernán Cortés after an Aztec uprising, during which many Spanish soldiers and Indigenous allies were killed.
aliases: La Noche Triste de la Conquista

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man asked permission to celebrate the Toxcatl [tosh-COT’ll] festival, where Pedro de Alvarado’s men committed a massacre on May 22, 1520. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Aztec emperor, the last to effectively rule the empire before the Spanish conquest.
parts.answer: Montezuma II (accept Moctezuma II; accept Moctezuma Xocoyotzin)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Montezuma was killed in the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan [ten-oak-teet-lan], whose ruins are now within this modern-day capital city.
parts.answer: Mexico City

parts.label: C
parts.question: Shortly after the death of Montezuma, Hernan Cortez ordered this secret escape from Tenochtitlan, in which hundreds of Spanish soldiers were killed.
parts.answer: La Noche Triste (accept the Night of Sorrows)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire, whose history is recorded in the Mendoza Codex, built artificial islands called chinampas for agriculture. This empire waged ritual Flower Wars against neighbors, such as Cholula and Tlaxcala. This Nahuatl-speaking empire had success against invaders on (*) La Noche Triste, but their capital was captured by Hernan Cortes in 1521. For 10 points, name this Mexican empire ruled by Montezuma, which was centered on Tenochtitlan.
parts.answer: Aztec Empire [or the Triple Alliance; or Excan Tlahtoloyan]

topics.description: Wu Zetian was the only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right, establishing the restored Zhou dynasty from 690 to 705 CE during the Tang period.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A consort from this dynasty claimed that she only needed an iron whip, an iron hammer, and a dagger to subdue a horse. The Silla kingdom sought this dynasty’s help in defeating Goguryeo, ending the Three Kingdoms of Korea period. A consort from this dynasty, (*) Yang Guifei, was put to death during a rebellion led by her adopted son. This dynasty was interrupted by the reign of the female emperor Wu Zetian. An Lushan led a rebellion during this dynasty, which succeeded the Sui. For 10 points, name this Chinese dynasty that ruled from 618 to 907 AD and saw the flourishing of poets like Du Fu and Li Bai.
parts.answer: Tang dynasty

parts.label: L
parts.question: This ruler once claimed that if she could not tame a horse with a whip, she would bludgeon its head with a hammer, and if it disobeyed further, she would cut its throat with a dagger. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this only legitimate female emperor of China, who interrupted the Tang dynasty to found a revived Zhou [“joe”] dynasty.
parts.answer: Wu Zetian [accept Empress Wu; or Wu Hou; or Wu Zhao]

parts.label: B
parts.question: In order to legitimize her power, Wu Zetian claimed to be a reincarnated bodhisattva from this religion’s Great Cloud Sutra text. This religion’s monasteries flourished during the Tang dynasty.
parts.answer: Buddhism [accept word forums such as Buddhist monasteries]

parts.label: C
parts.question: During her reign, Wu Zetian expanded this system for selecting government officials by merit in order to decrease the influence of the aristocracy in the government, opening the court to more commoners.
parts.answer: civil service examinations [accept imperial exam; accept keju]

topics.description: The natural animal fiber obtained primarily by shearing sheep, used in textiles, clothing, and historical trade.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A powerful family that ruled this city included men like Lorezno the Magnificent. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Italian city once ruled by the Medici family. This city is the most populous one in Tuscany.
parts.answer: Florence [or Firenze]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In 1378, Florence was the site of the Ciompi Revolt, initiated by disgruntled producers of this textile good, which comes from sheep.
parts.answer: wool

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While de facto ruler of Florence, Girolama Savonarola ordered one of these specific events to purge the city of sinful items like books, paintings, and musical instruments.
parts.answer: Bonfire of the Vanities [prompt on Bonfire]

topics.description: A country in northwestern Europe, historically associated with the Dutch Republic, major maritime and colonial activity, and cultural figures such as Rembrandt and Vermeer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After losing one conflict, the name of this tribe was banned and they were forced to assimilate into the Narragansett and Mohegan tribes. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this tribe, which fought the Massachusetts Bay Colony in a namesake 1630s war.
parts.answer: Pequot

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Pequots killed John Stone on this state’s namesake river, helping spark the war. The treaty that ended the war, which banned the Pequot language, was signed in this state’s capital of Hartford.
parts.answer: Connecticut [or the Connecticut River]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Before the English arrived in Connecticut, the Pequot primarily traded with merchants from this country, which sold New York to the British for not enough guilders.
parts.answer: Kingdom of The Netherlands [or Holland; Koninkrijk der Nederlanden]
